Hi Alex / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team received the high-level slides and have followed up with a more formal set of questions attached (polaris-iam-questions.xlsx). The focus areas are: SAML/OIDC SSO (SP and IdP flows), SCIM v2 provisioning, RBAC and delegated admin, privileged operations, and audit/logging for both hosted and private deployments.

Could you please:
- Confirm which specific SAML bindings and OIDC flows Redwood supports.
- Provide the SCIM schema mapping you use for user -> role -> groups and if you support bulk sync.
- Explain delegated admin and administrative separation (who can create roles, who can approve).
- Share sample audit log entries and retention policy for hosted and private customers.

We have a compliance checkpoint on Dec 15; ideally we’d have the completed control matrix + evidence by Dec 11 so our InfoSec can triage. If you need a short call to walk through items we can do that earlier.

Subject: Re: PolarisCorp - IAM control matrix & follow-ups

Hi Ellen — thanks for sending this over. We’ll take point on the matrix and can deliver the completed control matrix and supporting artifacts by COB Dec 11. Quick summary up front to help triage: 

- SAML: SP-initiated and IdP-initiated supported. SAML 2.0, HTTP-Redirect and HTTP-POST bindings. Metadata exchange via URL or file import. We support certificate rotation with a 30-day overlap window.
- OIDC: Authorization Code flow (PKCE), Client Credentials for machine-to-machine, and support for standard scopes. Dynamic client registration is supported in our Private offering; for hosted customers we register clients via the console/API.
- SCIM: SCIM v2 compliant endpoints. Supports create/read/update/delete for Users and Groups, incremental sync via change notifications, and a bulk import/export utility for initial onboard. Our role-to-group mapping is configurable; we typically map SCIM groups -> Redwood roles and sync group membership to role assignments.
- RBAC / Admin Controls: Role-based model with system roles (Org Admin, Billing Admin, ReadOnly) and custom roles. Delegated admin (scoped admin) is supported — admins can be limited by project/namespace. Role creation is restricted to Org Admins by default; you can enable a delegated role-manager role if you want non-org-admin users to create/edit roles.
- Audit & Logs: Token-level and request-level audit logs. For hosted customers we retain detailed logs for 90 days by default (extendable with add-on). Private deployments can be configured for customer-managed retention; sample log format attached.

I’ve attached the control matrix template we’ll fill out and an implementation guide with specifics (redwood-iam-control-matrix.xlsx, redwood-saml-oidc-implementation-guide.pdf). If you’re okay, we’ll fill the matrix and return with screenshots, API call examples, and a 30-line sample of audit log events.

Proposed next step: 30-minute deep-dive Dec 4 at 10:00 AM PT to walk through the SCIM mapping and delegated admin model.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alex — this is great, thanks. A couple of clarifying points from our InfoSec (copied):

1) Delegated admin: we need to see a demo or screenshots showing separation of duties — specifically the ability to create roles without granting permission to manage billing or change tenant-wide auth settings.
2) SCIM bulk import: do you support attribute transformations (e.g., mapping samaccountname -> username, normalizing email domains) during sync? If not, do you provide a pre-processing script?
3) Audit logs: we need a sample that shows userId, actor, action, resourceId, timestamp, IP, and whether the action was allowed/denied. Also retention proof — any SOC2 attachments that reference log retention are helpful.

Would DOM (Director of IT Ops) be able to join the Dec 4 meeting? They prefer Dec 4 at 11:00 AM PT instead.

Thanks — Ellen

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clarifying questions and for moving the meeting to 11:00 AM PT. Ben and I recorded a short set of screenshots and exports we think will answer the immediate checklist items and we’ve completed the control matrix you sent. Highlights below and what we attached: control matrix (completed), 30-line audit log sample, SCIM mapping example, and a short video walkthrough link.

Highlights / answers:
- Delegated admin: We demonstrate a role-manager role that can create/edit roles scoped to a project namespace without access to tenant-level settings or billing. Screenshot: Admin -> Roles -> Create Role (attached). Default behavior: only Org Admins can change authentication configuration (SAML/OIDC metadata).
- SCIM attribute transforms: Redwood offers attribute mapping rules in the provisioning UI (rename, regex normalization, domain-rewrite). For more complex transforms customers can run a pre-processing Lambda in our Private deployment or use the SCIM bulk import script we provided. Example mapping attached.
- Audit log sample: attached file contains fields: timestamp, actor_user_id, actor_email, action, resource_type, resource_id, ip_address, outcome (allowed/denied), request_id. For hosted customers, standard retention 90 days; we can export raw logs for compliance or extend retention via Enterprise add-on. We are happy to include SOC2 audit statement references — please let us know the exact evidence you need and we’ll pull the right artifacts from our compliance pack.

Attachments: redwood-iam-control-matrix.xlsx (completed), audit-log-sample.txt, scim-mapping-example.json, screenshots.zip
